summary: holdover chunk skips during sse backpressure on long responses
description: Issue summary: Customer reports that for long-running SSE streams (>45s), when the client is slow to read (simulate high CPU or network jitter), the resumed stream after a transient disconnect is missing intermediate 'choice' chunks. Impact: Some end-users see partial completions (missing sentences) causing downstream application state to appear truncated. Environment: Dedicated account (DialogueAI), prod us-east region, using pinned model llm-redwood-13b-realtime on dedicated pool. Steps to reproduce: 1) Start generation with a prompt that produces ~1200 tokens (long narrative). 2) Simulate client-side backpressure by throttling the socket read or introducing 250-500ms pauses every 5s. 3) Force a short disconnect (TCP RST or browser tab backgrounding). 4) Reconnect and observe SSE stream resume events. Observed behavior: Resume occurs but intermediate choice chunks appear to be skipped; final choice present but continuity has gaps (missing sentences). Sometimes the reconstructed text contains duplicated fragments later in stream, as if fragments were re-ordered. Expected behavior: Resume should yield a stitched stream with no lost tokens and preserved order. Logs/trace: Edge proxy logs show repeated 503s then 200 on reconnect. Serving runtime trace shows successful KV-cache retrieval and a resume token match but there are gap warnings in the stitcher: "stitcher: missing-offset gap detected, dropping N fragments". Temporary workaround provided: Customer reduced concurrency and enabled application-level buffering (hold fragments until final event). Request: Support asked for an engineering investigation into whether edge-proxy backpressure triggers drop of partially-committed fragments and whether stitcher heuristics can be relaxed for dedicated pools.

investigation_notes: Hypothesis A: Edge proxy coalescing + upstream backpressure leads to partial fragment write that is GC'd by stitcher on reconnect. Check proxy buffer window and flush semantics.

Hypothesis B: Stitcher uses strict offset continuity; in dedicated pool with heavy KV-cache hits, re-attach can jump offsets and the heuristic treats the mismatch as duplication risk and drops fragments.
Actions taken: reproduced with supplied throttle script; captured runtime trace with debug stitcher logs; instrumented fragment-hold-time metric (pending PR).
Dashboards referenced: Streaming Latency (console/streams/us-east), stitcher-error-rate (grafana), edge-proxy-buffer-occupancy (grafana).
Related PRs/branches: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/4218 (instrumentation); follow-up patch planned to tweak stitch_timeout and add tolerant reordering window.
Linked tickets: SUP-4721 (similar SSE resume truncation reported previously), SUP-72401 (orphan end-event after browser refresh behind proxy).
resolution_notes: In Progress - Engineering to land a two-part change: (1) increase stitcher tolerance window from 150ms to 500ms on dedicated pools and expose feature flag; (2) modify edge-proxy to flush partially accumulated fragments when a resume/reconnect is detected. Temporary mitigation (customer applied): lower keepalive and enable buffer-forwarding on proxy which reduced incidence from ~10% to ~3%. Next steps: land PR 4218 for metrics, follow with PR to add tolerant stitching behavior, schedule patch in canary for us-east. If successful, roll to Dedicated pools. No customer data loss has been logged beyond truncated user-visible output.
